jobs.title: Director of Advancement
jobs.description:
APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS:
To apply, please send a cover letter and resume in PDF format to jobs@aiany.org. Please put the job title and your last name on the subject line of your email. No phone calls, please. 

Company Description

The American Institute of Architects New York (AIANY), established in 1857, is the oldest and largest chapter of the American Institute of Architects, with over 5,500 members including architects, allied professionals, students, and design enthusiasts. In partnership with the Center for Architecture, it serves as a cultural hub for architecture and urbanism in New York City, offering exhibitions, public programs, and design education. The Center for Architecture hosts the annual Archtober festival and fosters collaboration among design, development, and policy sectors. Together, AIANY and the Center aim to promote design excellence, expand public knowledge, and inspire innovation in the built environment.

Position Overview

AIA New York and the Center for Architecture seek a strategic, entrepreneurial, and relationship-driven Director of Advancement to lead the organizations’ advancement, partnership, and revenue-development strategy. Reporting to the Executive Director and serving as a member of the senior leadership team, the Director will identify and grow revenue opportunities across corporate sponsorship and partnerships, foundation and government support, individual philanthropy, special initiatives, and other emerging opportunities.

This is a broad and entrepreneurial advancement role. The Director will work across the organizations’ programs, audiences, relationships, communications platforms, and institutional assets to identify new opportunities for revenue and partnership, while strengthening existing sources of contributed support. Particular emphasis will be placed on expanding corporate and institutional relationships and developing sustainable revenue models that extend beyond traditional fundraising events.

The Director will also play a central role in Board relations and development and will partner closely with the Communications and Marketing team to strengthen institutional visibility, articulate the value of the organizations’ work to external audiences, and develop compelling opportunities for partners and supporters.

The ideal candidate is a strategic generalist who combines strong relationship-building and fundraising skills with business-development instincts, creativity, and an ability to recognize opportunities across different areas of an organization. They will be comfortable moving between high-level strategy and execution, building relationships across sectors, engaging Board and volunteer leadership, and working collaboratively across departments to translate ideas and relationships into sustainable sources of support.

Key Responsibilities & Essential Functions

Advancement, Partnerships & Revenue Strategy

Lead an organization-wide advancement and revenue-development strategy, with particular emphasis on corporate and institutional support, sponsorship, and strategic partnerships.

Identify, develop, and test new revenue opportunities across AIA New York and the Center for Architecture’s programs, audiences, events, exhibitions, educational initiatives, communications platforms, and institutional relationships.

Build and manage a robust pipeline of corporate partners and sponsors, developing relationships that extend beyond transactional or event-based sponsorship.

Develop customized partnership opportunities that connect corporate and institutional priorities with the organizations’ mission, programs, audiences, expertise, and visibility.

Partner with program and senior leadership to assess the revenue potential of new and existing initiatives and develop appropriate funding and partnership models.

Expand corporate sponsorship and partnership support for key institutional initiatives, including Archtober, Learning & Engagement programs, Exhibitions, and other mission-driven programs.

Oversee foundation and government fundraising strategy, working closely with the Grants Manager to identify opportunities and develop compelling institutional proposals.

Oversee individual giving and major gifts strategy, ensuring effective cultivation and stewardship while identifying opportunities for sustainable growth.

Lead the continued evolution of fundraising events as one component of a diversified advancement strategy, with an emphasis on expanding revenue sources beyond event-driven fundraising.

Partner with the Executive Director on high-level cultivation, solicitation, business development, and strategic partnership opportunities.

Manage and mentor the Development team, including two full-time Development Managers and one part-time Grants Manager.

Establish and track revenue goals, pipelines, forecasts, and performance across advancement activities, evaluating results and adjusting strategies as appropriate.

Communications, Marketing & External Engagement

Partner closely with the Communications and Marketing team to develop strategies that strengthen institutional visibility, audience engagement, partnership opportunities, and revenue generation.

Ensure alignment between advancement priorities and organizational communications, including positioning programs and initiatives effectively for corporate, institutional, philanthropic, and public audiences.

Collaborate on the development of sponsorship materials, institutional messaging, campaigns, and other communications that support revenue and partnership goals.

Identify opportunities to leverage AIA New York and the Center for Architecture’s brand, audiences, programs, communications platforms, expertise, and convening power to create value for partners and supporters.

Build and maintain relationships with institutional, corporate, civic, cultural, philanthropic, and community partners that advance organizational visibility, impact, and sustainability.

Serve as a senior ambassador for AIA New York and the Center for Architecture within the architecture, design, real estate, cultural, corporate, philanthropic, and civic communities.

Board Relations & Leadership

Serve as a key staff liaison to the Center for Architecture Board, working closely with the Executive Director and Board leadership on institutional strategy, advancement, partnerships, and Board engagement.

Lead and coordinate Board committee activities related to fundraising, advancement, and institutional development.

Develop meaningful opportunities for Board members to participate in relationship-building, fundraising, sponsorship development, and institutional partnerships.

Partner with the Executive Director and Board leadership on Board development, including identifying and cultivating prospective Board members and volunteer leaders who can expand the organizations’ networks, expertise, and capacity.

Equip Board members and other volunteer leaders with the information, materials, and strategies needed to serve effectively as ambassadors for the organizations.

Foster strong relationships with Board members and other key stakeholders, ensuring consistent communication and engagement around organizational priorities.

Qualifications 

Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred
Minimum of 8 years of progressive advancement, development, or fundraising experience, including at least 5 years in a leadership role
Demonstrated success growing contributed revenue through individual giving, sponsorships, foundations, or major fundraising initiatives
Experience managing donor relationships, fundraising campaigns, and strategic partnerships
Strong leadership and team management skills with experience developing high-performing teams
Excellent communication, presentation, and relationship management skills
Experience working with boards, committees, and senior stakeholders 

Additional Information

Location: 
This is a predominantly in person role, with some remote work possible (up to approx. 2 days per week, depending on event and programmatic needs on site) 
FLSA Classification: 
   Full-Time, Exempt 
Salary Range:
$130,000 - $140,000 
Position Reports to:
Executive Director  

Benefits:
We offer a competitive benefits package including low or zero cost health, dental and vision insurance options, 3% 401k match, 15 days PTO per year in your first five years (20 days after five years), 10 paid holidays, Summer Fridays, and the last week of the year off. 
Physical Demands: Some lifting (up to 30 lbs.). Prolonged periods of standing and/or walking. 

AIANY and the Center for Architecture is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to providing an environment of mutual respect where equal employment opportunities are available to all applicants and existing employees without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy (including childbirth, lactation and related medical conditions), national origin, citizenship status, age, physical and mental disability, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information (including characteristics and testing), military and veteran status, or any protected category prohibited by local, state or federal laws.

jobs.title: Deputy Director
jobs.description:
Company Description

The Detroit Health Department has served Detroiters for more than a century. Today, DHD is building a modern public health department that is visible, responsive, data-informed, and rooted in the daily realities of Detroit residents. Our work goes beyond traditional health services. Through a Health in All Policies approach, DHD recognizes that health is shaped by housing, transportation, environmental conditions, economic opportunity, public safety, education, and the broader systems that shape life in the city. We seek team members who can work across programs, City departments, and community partners to improve health, reduce inequities, and deliver better outcomes for Detroit residents.

Role Description
Deputy Public Health Director (Chief of Staff) On-Site Detroit, MI

The Detroit Health Department seeks a strategic, highly organized leader to serve as Deputy Director (Chief of Staff). Reporting to the Chief Public Health Officer, this leader will help set priorities, coordinate the department’s agenda, and ensure that decisions lead to action and measurable results for Detroit residents.

The Chief of Staff works closely with the department’s other Deputy Director and senior leaders to connect policy, programs, administration, and City partnerships. The role focuses on executive coordination, clear communication, and follow-through across the department.

We are looking for someone who can understand complex issues, ask thoughtful questions, write clearly, build trust, and get work done. This is a hands-on executive leadership role for someone who can move between long-term strategy and day-to-day problem-solving while keeping the needs of residents at the center.

Examples of Duties

Turn the Chief Public Health Officer’s priorities into work plans with clear responsibilities, deadlines, and measures of progress. Track commitments and bring forward decisions that need leadership attention.
Lead executive coordination, including leadership meeting agendas, briefing materials, decision records, and follow-up. Ensure meetings produce clear decisions and next steps.
Work with the other Deputy Director and senior leaders to resolve problems that cross programs or divisions, reduce duplication, and keep shared priorities moving.
Prepare and review policy briefs, decision memos, presentations, and correspondence. Bring together program data, operational needs, and community perspectives to help leadership evaluate options.
Coordinate progress on the department’s strategic agenda, including special projects and Health in All Policies initiatives. Help align departmental work with City priorities and commitments to residents.
Build effective relationships with the Mayor’s Office, City departments, public agencies, and community partners. Represent the Chief Public Health Officer in meetings and initiatives when designated.
Work with administrative, finance, human resources, legal, and program leaders to address staffing, funding, agreement, and implementation issues that require executive coordination.
Supervise assigned staff, establish clear expectations, support professional growth, and strengthen a culture of collaboration, accountability, and respect.

Minimum Qualifications

Master’s degree in Public Health required.
Minimum ten (10) years of professional experience working in complex organizational environments preferably including full time public health administrative experience.

Preferred Qualifications:

At least five years of executive-level operations or strategic management experience.
Experience coordinating executive priorities, leading work across teams, and improving performance in government, public health, or a similarly complex organization.
Strong writing, judgment, facilitation, and relationship-building skills, with a demonstrated commitment to public service and health equity.
Equivalent combinations of education and experience may be substituted to meet the education and experience requirements of this position.

Available Light Theatre (AVLT) seeks a Managing Director
to oversee operations, financial management, and strategic execution in collaboration with the Artistic Director and Board of Directors. This contract position reports directly to the Board of Directors. The Managing Director plays a critical role in supporting the art of AVLT by ensuring the successful and efficient day-to-day operations of an ensemble-led company that seeks to create joyful, profound theatre. The rate of pay for this contract position is $32,000 annual salary
, with an expected workload of an average of 20 hours per week

About Available Light Theatre

Celebrating its 20th season, Available Light Theatre is a professional 501(c)(3) non-profit, non-Equity ensemble theatre company in downtown Columbus, Ohio. Mixing original and contemporary works, AVLT usually produces a season of 3-4 shows, typically running from September to June. jobs.title: Executive Director, Application Development – Telematics (P&C Insurance Technology)
jobs.description:
Why USAA?

At USAA, our mission is to empower our members to achieve financial security through highly competitive products, exceptional service and trusted advice. We seek to be the #1 choice for the military community and their families.

Embrace a fulfilling career at USAA, where our core values – honesty, integrity, loyalty and service – define how we treat each other and our members. Be part of what truly makes us special and impactful.

We are proud to support active-duty military spouses. USAA roles may offer remote or hybrid flexibility for active-duty military spouses consistent with applicable policy and business needs.

The Opportunity

This is far more than an application development leadership role. It is an opportunity to help shape the future of how USAA understands risk, serves members, and competes in an increasingly data-driven insurance marketplace.

As Executive Director, Application Development - Telematics
, you will report directly to the AVP of P&C Policy Core Systems and Technical Services and lead a growing organization of approximately 45 employees and 50 contractor resources responsible for one of USAA's most strategically important and rapidly evolving technology capabilities. Reporting to Aaron Bend, AVP of Policy Core Systems and Technical Services, you will own the technology strategy, architecture, engineering delivery, and future evolution of USAA's telematics ecosystem, helping transform vast amounts of driving behavior, connected vehicle, mobile application, and sensor data into actionable insights that improve pricing accuracy, claims outcomes, risk segmentation, fraud detection, member experiences, and overall business performance.

The timing of this opportunity is particularly compelling. Telematics has evolved from a niche capability into a foundational component of USAA's Personal Auto business. Today, telematics data influences pricing decisions on more than half of USAA's quoted and issued auto insurance policies, and the organization continues to invest aggressively in expanding telematics-driven capabilities across pricing, underwriting, claims, and member engagement. Through strategic partnerships with telematics providers, automotive OEMs, and leading technology partners, USAA is accelerating its ability to leverage real-time data to create a more personalized, proactive, and intelligent insurance experience.

The Executive Director will play a central role in advancing cloud-native technologies, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and advanced analytics to unlock new sources of business value from telematics data. The role will help expand the use of telematics beyond pricing and underwriting into areas such as claims automation, crash detection, first-notice-of-loss acceleration, risk prevention, and member engagement, while also supporting the long-term evolution of USAA's telematics platform and data ecosystem.

Looking ahead, this position offers the opportunity to influence how USAA evolves beyond traditional telematics into a broader connected ecosystem. As connected vehicles, smart devices, sensors, and Internet of Things technologies continue to reshape the industry, USAA is exploring new ways to leverage data to improve member outcomes across both Auto and Property insurance, including Connected Home capabilities designed to proactively help members prevent losses before they occur.

For accomplished technology leaders from leading insurers, telematics providers, connected vehicle platforms, mobility technology companies, or other data-driven organizations, this represents a rare opportunity to move beyond managing an established program and help define the future direction of an increasingly strategic enterprise capability. The successful candidate will influence multi-year business and technology roadmaps, partner directly with senior leaders across technology and the business, and help determine how telematics, artificial intelligence, and emerging data ecosystems shape the future of insurance at USAA.

Few opportunities offer this combination of strategic visibility, technical complexity, business impact, and innovation. The work spans cloud modernization, AI, machine learning, mobile technologies, data engineering, vehicle integrations, digital experiences, pricing, underwriting, claims, and connected-device ecosystems, all within an organization making significant long-term investments in these capabilities.

For executives who are already successful and not actively considering a career move, this opportunity offers something increasingly rare: the chance to build and scale a transformative capability at an organization where telematics is already influencing core business decisions and is expected to play an even larger role in the future. The leader selected for this role will have a unique opportunity to help define how USAA leverages connected data, advanced analytics, and emerging technologies to better serve millions of members and strengthen its competitive position for years to come.

Executive Directors in Application Development plan, coordinate, and supervise all activities related to the design, development, and implementation and maintenance of the organization's applications development and analysis function. These leaders also manage multiple development teams often supporting one or more lines of business or business functional areas. Additionally, these leaders work closely with clients in order to map and support their operational needs. These leaders are also responsible for developing, distributing, supporting, enforcing, and integrating best practices and technology standards across the organization, including ensuring all Information Technology General Controls, processes and procedures are followed as applicable and appropriate.

Location

USAA offers a flexible work environment that requires an individual to be in the office 4 days per week. This position can be based in one of the following locations: Plano, TX (preference) or San Antonio, TX. Relocation assistance is available for this position.

What You'll Do

Perform workload management and prioritization duties in support of operations for the functional area assigned.
Apply subject-matter-expert functional knowledge to lead subordinate workers in producing work deliverables in support of departmental initiatives.
Develop functional policies, procedures and guidelines.
Identify opportunities and facilitates major improvements to processes and systems.
Ensure that the assigned application group develops processes and tools that contribute to the company business objectives.
Ensure that all application processes developed internally or by external service providers are conducted in line with corporate social responsibility, environmental and technical policies and applicable standards and legislation.
Oversee the assessment of the technical and business fitness of the application portfolio and their associated costs and risks In partnership with CTO, Infrastructure and IT Security, and ensure that the organization's applications are effectively secured and that risks are mitigated and comply with legal and corporate privacy and confidentiality rules.
Establish management routines to ensure appropriate oversight of the organization's software development and maintenance activities.
Serve as financial steward for the organization and manage relationships with major vendors and service providers to ensure they cost-effectively meet the needs of the organization.
Evaluate and select third party vendors to provide value added services.
Facilitate the contracting process through the Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) enterprise process.
Responsible for contract company/service performance providing timely feedback to ensure the best value for USAA.
Collaborate with CTO to ensure that solutions are consistent with technology standards.
Work across IT and business partners to reduce technical debt.
Collaborate with other leaders and/or stakeholders and develop an application development strategy that aligns with business strategy, adds value and is within budget constraints.
Responsible for team's adherence to SDLC and applicable controls.
Work to ensure teams have appropriate, development plans consistent with domain of expertise.
Mentor across the technical community.
Provide oversight to the engagement with the business DPO and ensure deliverables adhere to Agile practices / methodologies.
Ensure risks associated with business activities are effectively identified, measured, monitored, and controlled in accordance with risk and compliance policies and procedures.

What You Have

Bachelors degree in Computer Science, I.S., or related field; OR 4 years of relevant education and/or experience.
10 years of experience of general IT management competencies.
4 years of people leadership experience in building, managing and/or developing high-performing teams required.
Strong technical background of web-based application architecture, system and database architecture, security application integration and object-oriented languages in a large enterprise environment.
Experience in all stages of the SDLC: requirements gathering, design, development, testing, and implementation.
Demonstrated ability to communicate technical information to a non-technical audience.
Experience collaborating with resources and stakeholders, influencing decisions and managing work to achieve strategic goals.
Experienced in vendor contract management and management of distributed development teams and resources.
Financial acumen involving budgets, forecasting, and executing on the budgets for applicable technology support function.
Understanding of relevant industry frameworks (e.g., COBIT, ITIL, SAFe, etc.)
Understanding of Legislative and Regulatory Compliance Requirements.
Experience overseeing the technology life cycle from requirements analysis, feasibility estimates, design, code, documentation, testing, implementation, and support.
Technical knowledge and understanding of technical domains that reside within Infrastructure Services, Security, Data or Application Development.
Experience conducting cost benefit analyses and leveraging results to drive technology support solutions.
Demonstrated thought leadership in embedding intuitive story telling of technology support functions including concise presentation of complex technical details.
Experience and ability to drive a culture of quality and personal accountability through technology support teams.

What Sets You Apart

5+ years of experience in behavior and usage-based insurance technology or telematics programs.
3+ years of experience modernizing legacy insurance systems to public cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, GCP, Azure).
Domain experience with usage-based and behavior-based insurance, personal lines insurance, and personal lines claims.
Experience leading the technical strategy and delivery of telematics solutions for P&C, maintaining and building relationships with ecosystem partners, and translating telematic data into higher value using AI.
Experience partnering with business stakeholders in building multi-year roadmaps across P&C functional areas to advance the telematics architecture that supports multi-product capabilities.
Experience scaling data platforms that ingest massive telematics streams (e.g., Mobile app data, IoT device data, OEM vehicle data) and using near real-time data for multiple insurance use cases.
Experience building mobile app experiences tailored to telematic insurance programs.
Experience partnering with key industry telematic suppliers (e.g., CMT, Arity, Okto) or vehicle OEMs.
Experience using machine learning or advanced models to turn telematics data into risk scoring, analytical insights, pricing segmentation, claims detection, or customer engagement tools.
Experience leading the technical strategy to deliver telematic solutions at top insurance carriers.

Visa Sponsor

jobs.title: Director of Communications and Marketing
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE COMMUNICATIONS AND MARKETING DIRECTOR POSITION

The Communications and Marketing Director for the City of Greensboro is a
dynamic executive leadership role for a strategic communicator who wants to make a meaningful impact on an entire community. This position leads the City’s comprehensive communications and marketing efforts, shaping how residents, businesses, visitors, and stakeholders experience and understand their local government.

Reporting to an Assistant City Manager, the Director will oversee the City’s full spectrum of communications operations — including internal and external communications, marketing, Greensboro Television Network, the contact center, and print shop/mail services. This individual will work directly with elected officials, the City Manager’s Office, and department leaders to develop forward-thinking strategies, address emerging issues, and deliver clear, compelling messages that tell Greensboro’s story with accuracy and transparency.

The Director will elevate and strengthen content creation standards across the organization, setting clear expectations for high-quality, strategic, and consistent communications. This includes overseeing multi-platform writing and digital content production that effectively reaches audiences across websites, email communications, social media channels, video platforms, and emerging digital tools. The Director will ensure messaging is tailored appropriately for each platform while maintaining a cohesive and recognizable City brand voice.

In addition to written communications, the Director will oversee comprehensive digital content production, including multimedia storytelling, visual design standards, video messaging, and web content optimization. The role requires ensuring that content is accessible, engaging, and aligned with best practices in digital communication, including search optimization and usability standards.

A strong candidate will bring a data-driven mindset to the organization. The Communications and Marketing Director will leverage analytical tools and performance metrics to guide strategy, evaluate impact, and inform decision-making. This includes utilizing website and social media analytics, engagement metrics, sentiment analysis, and audience insights to refine messaging and outreach efforts. The Director will oversee proactive social media management strategies, including content planning, scheduling, real-time engagement, performance tracking, and continuous improvement informed by analytics. By grounding communications strategies in data, the Director will ensure resources are allocated effectively and messaging resonates with diverse audiences across the community.

The Director must also demonstrate exceptional skill in translating complex, technical, or policy-driven information into clear, accessible, and audience-centered messaging. Whether communicating budget priorities, infrastructure projects, public safety initiatives, or crisis updates, the Director will ensure that information is presented in ways that are transparent, understandable, and meaningful to residents and stakeholders.

The Communications and Marketing Director will serve as the steward of the City’s brand — ensuring that all messaging strengthens public trust, enhances reputation, and reflects the City’s values and priorities. This includes creating proactive, analytics-informed communications that engage residents, visitors, and business owners, as well as leading communications during high-profile initiatives, major events, and crisis situations with real-time monitoring and strategic responsiveness.

Additionally, the Communications and Marketing Director will provide the vision and strategic leadership to guide the Communications team through change and modernization. The Director will foster a culture of innovation, empowering staff to explore new ideas, communication approaches, and technologies that strengthen the reach and impact of the City’s communications program. Through intentional coaching, mentoring, and professional development, the Director will build staff capabilities and enhance the department’s overall effectiveness.

As a key member of the City Manager’s leadership team, the Director will collaborate across departments and with elected leadership to help shape programs, services, and community initiatives that advance organizational goals and improve quality of life for the people of Greensboro.

This Exempt position offers the opportunity to lead a talented team, influence citywide strategy, and play a central role in building an informed, connected, and engaged community.

ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION

The City of Greensboro is governed under a Council-Manager form of government, with the council serving as the legislative body of City government. City council is composed of a mayor and eight council members who serve four-year terms. The council is responsible for setting and directing policy regarding operations of City government, as well as approving the City’s budget of $909.8M, which supports 3,063 full-time, 59 part-time, and up to 681 temporary and seasonal employees across many departments. The City Manager serves as the chief executive officer of the City and is responsible for the execution of council policy and for the management of day-to-day City government operations.

Learn more about the City of Greensboro by visiting its website.

COMPENSATION INFORMATION

The full salary range for the position is $119,856-$214,479 with eligibility for additional executive compensation of $4,320 annually. As a City employee, the Communications and Marketing Director participates in the North Carolina Local Governmental Employees’ Retirement System (NCLGERS), which includes a 6% pre-tax employee contribution and a City-funded employer contribution, with vesting after five years.

Supplemental retirement savings opportunities include participation in a 401(a) plan with a 3.25% City contribution based on base salary, as well as 457 / Roth 457 and 401(k) / Roth 401(k) plans. For highly experienced executives, the City may recognize prior public sector service through adjusted leave accrual rates and initial leave balances, consistent with established policies. Learn more about the City’s generous benefits package here.

As with all individuals appointed as City Department Directors, the Communications and Marketing Director must live within a 30-mile radius of the Greensboro city limits within 12 months of their appointment.

QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor’s Degree and 7 or more years of experience in communications and marketing, preferably within the non-profit government sector OR Associate’s Degree and 10 or more years of experience in the above mentioned areas
Minimum of 5 years of supervision/management of teams engaged in corporate communications, public relations, video production and/or social media

An Ideal Candidate Would Also Possess (Preferred Qualifications):

Budget management/financial management experience
Municipal government management experience at the senior or executive level
Prior media and publication experience
Expertise in crisis communications
Ability to effectively manage through change, modernization, and departmental transformation

TO APPLY

Please submit your application along with a resume, cover letter, and reference information to the City of Greensboro, NC application located here: Greensboro Communications and Marketing Director Application. The application deadline is October 11th, with final review of applications occurring the week of October 19th.

They will be comfortable moving between high-level strategy and execution, building relationships across sectors, engaging Board and volunteer leadership, and working collaboratively across departments to translate ideas and relationships into sustainable sources of support.

Key Responsibilities & Essential Functions

Advancement, Partnerships & Revenue Strategy

Lead an organization-wide advancement and revenue-development strategy, with particular emphasis on corporate and institutional support, sponsorship, and strategic partnerships.

Identify, develop, and test new revenue opportunities across AIA New York and the Center for Architecture’s programs, audiences, events, exhibitions, educational initiatives, communications platforms, and institutional relationships.

Build and manage a robust pipeline of corporate partners and sponsors, developing relationships that extend beyond transactional or event-based sponsorship.

Develop customized partnership opportunities that connect corporate and institutional priorities with the organizations’ mission, programs, audiences, expertise, and visibility.

Partner with program and senior leadership to assess the revenue potential of new and existing initiatives and develop appropriate funding and partnership models.

Expand corporate sponsorship and partnership support for key institutional initiatives, including Archtober, Learning & Engagement programs, Exhibitions, and other mission-driven programs.

Oversee foundation and government fundraising strategy, working closely with the Grants Manager to identify opportunities and develop compelling institutional proposals.

Oversee individual giving and major gifts strategy, ensuring effective cultivation and stewardship while identifying opportunities for sustainable growth.

Lead the continued evolution of fundraising events as one component of a diversified advancement strategy, with an emphasis on expanding revenue sources beyond event-driven fundraising.

Partner with the Executive Director on high-level cultivation, solicitation, business development, and strategic partnership opportunities.

Manage and mentor the Development team, including two full-time Development Managers and one part-time Grants Manager.

Establish and track revenue goals, pipelines, forecasts, and performance across advancement activities, evaluating results and adjusting strategies as appropriate.

Communications, Marketing & External Engagement

Partner closely with the Communications and Marketing team to develop strategies that strengthen institutional visibility, audience engagement, partnership opportunities, and revenue generation.

Ensure alignment between advancement priorities and organizational communications, including positioning programs and initiatives effectively for corporate, institutional, philanthropic, and public audiences.

Collaborate on the development of sponsorship materials, institutional messaging, campaigns, and other communications that support revenue and partnership goals.

Identify opportunities to leverage AIA New York and the Center for Architecture’s brand, audiences, programs, communications platforms, expertise, and convening power to create value for partners and supporters.

Build and maintain relationships with institutional, corporate, civic, cultural, philanthropic, and community partners that advance organizational visibility, impact, and sustainability.

Serve as a senior ambassador for AIA New York and the Center for Architecture within the architecture, design, real estate, cultural, corporate, philanthropic, and civic communities.

Board Relations & Leadership

Serve as a key staff liaison to the Center for Architecture Board, working closely with the Executive Director and Board leadership on institutional strategy, advancement, partnerships, and Board engagement.

Lead and coordinate Board committee activities related to fundraising, advancement, and institutional development.

Develop meaningful opportunities for Board members to participate in relationship-building, fundraising, sponsorship development, and institutional partnerships.

Partner with the Executive Director and Board leadership on Board development, including identifying and cultivating prospective Board members and volunteer leaders who can expand the organizations’ networks, expertise, and capacity.

Equip Board members and other volunteer leaders with the information, materials, and strategies needed to serve effectively as ambassadors for the organizations.

Foster strong relationships with Board members and other key stakeholders, ensuring consistent communication and engagement around organizational priorities.

Qualifications 

Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred
Minimum of 8 years of progressive advancement, development, or fundraising experience, including at least 5 years in a leadership role
Demonstrated success growing contributed revenue through individual giving, sponsorships, foundations, or major fundraising initiatives
Experience managing donor relationships, fundraising campaigns, and strategic partnerships
Strong leadership and team management skills with experience developing high-performing teams
Excellent communication, presentation, and relationship management skills
Experience working with boards, committees, and senior stakeholders

Company Description

The Detroit Health Department has served Detroiters for more than a century. Today, DHD is building a modern public health department that is visible, responsive, data-informed, and rooted in the daily realities of Detroit residents. Our work goes beyond traditional health services. Through a Health in All Policies approach, DHD recognizes that health is shaped by housing, transportation, environmental conditions, economic opportunity, public safety, education, and the broader systems that shape life in the city. We seek team members who can work across programs, City departments, and community partners to improve health, reduce inequities, and deliver better outcomes for Detroit residents.

Role Description
Deputy Public Health Director (Chief of Staff) On-Site Detroit, MI

The Detroit Health Department seeks a strategic, highly organized leader to serve as Deputy Director (Chief of Staff). Reporting to the Chief Public Health Officer, this leader will help set priorities, coordinate the department’s agenda, and ensure that decisions lead to action and measurable results for Detroit residents.

The Chief of Staff works closely with the department’s other Deputy Director and senior leaders to connect policy, programs, administration, and City partnerships. The role focuses on executive coordination, clear communication, and follow-through across the department.

We are looking for someone who can understand complex issues, ask thoughtful questions, write clearly, build trust, and get work done. This is a hands-on executive leadership role for someone who can move between long-term strategy and day-to-day problem-solving while keeping the needs of residents at the center.

Examples of Duties

Turn the Chief Public Health Officer’s priorities into work plans with clear responsibilities, deadlines, and measures of progress. Track commitments and bring forward decisions that need leadership attention.
Lead executive coordination, including leadership meeting agendas, briefing materials, decision records, and follow-up. Ensure meetings produce clear decisions and next steps.
Work with the other Deputy Director and senior leaders to resolve problems that cross programs or divisions, reduce duplication, and keep shared priorities moving.
Prepare and review policy briefs, decision memos, presentations, and correspondence. Bring together program data, operational needs, and community perspectives to help leadership evaluate options.
Coordinate progress on the department’s strategic agenda, including special projects and Health in All Policies initiatives. Help align departmental work with City priorities and commitments to residents.
Build effective relationships with the Mayor’s Office, City departments, public agencies, and community partners. Represent the Chief Public Health Officer in meetings and initiatives when designated.
Work with administrative, finance, human resources, legal, and program leaders to address staffing, funding, agreement, and implementation issues that require executive coordination.
Supervise assigned staff, establish clear expectations, support professional growth, and strengthen a culture of collaboration, accountability, and respect.

Minimum Qualifications

Master’s degree in Public Health required.
Minimum ten (10) years of professional experience working in complex organizational environments preferably including full time public health administrative experience.

Preferred Qualifications:

At least five years of executive-level operations or strategic management experience.
Experience coordinating executive priorities, leading work across teams, and improving performance in government, public health, or a similarly complex organization.
Strong writing, judgment, facilitation, and relationship-building skills, with a demonstrated commitment to public service and health equity.
Equivalent combinations of education and experience may be substituted to meet the education and experience requirements of this position.

new_jobs.title: Executive Director, Application Development – Telematics (P&C Insurance Technology)
new_jobs.description:
Why USAA?

At USAA, our mission is to empower our members to achieve financial security through highly competitive products, exceptional service and trusted advice. We seek to be the #1 choice for the military community and their families.

Embrace a fulfilling career at USAA, where our core values – honesty, integrity, loyalty and service – define how we treat each other and our members. Be part of what truly makes us special and impactful.

We are proud to support active-duty military spouses. USAA roles may offer remote or hybrid flexibility for active-duty military spouses consistent with applicable policy and business needs.

The Opportunity

This is far more than an application development leadership role. It is an opportunity to help shape the future of how USAA understands risk, serves members, and competes in an increasingly data-driven insurance marketplace.

As Executive Director, Application Development - Telematics
, you will report directly to the AVP of P&C Policy Core Systems and Technical Services and lead a growing organization of approximately 45 employees and 50 contractor resources responsible for one of USAA's most strategically important and rapidly evolving technology capabilities. Reporting to Aaron Bend, AVP of Policy Core Systems and Technical Services, you will own the technology strategy, architecture, engineering delivery, and future evolution of USAA's telematics ecosystem, helping transform vast amounts of driving behavior, connected vehicle, mobile application, and sensor data into actionable insights that improve pricing accuracy, claims outcomes, risk segmentation, fraud detection, member experiences, and overall business performance.

The timing of this opportunity is particularly compelling. Telematics has evolved from a niche capability into a foundational component of USAA's Personal Auto business. Today, telematics data influences pricing decisions on more than half of USAA's quoted and issued auto insurance policies, and the organization continues to invest aggressively in expanding telematics-driven capabilities across pricing, underwriting, claims, and member engagement. Through strategic partnerships with telematics providers, automotive OEMs, and leading technology partners, USAA is accelerating its ability to leverage real-time data to create a more personalized, proactive, and intelligent insurance experience.

The Executive Director will play a central role in advancing cloud-native technologies, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and advanced analytics to unlock new sources of business value from telematics data. The role will help expand the use of telematics beyond pricing and underwriting into areas such as claims automation, crash detection, first-notice-of-loss acceleration, risk prevention, and member engagement, while also supporting the long-term evolution of USAA's telematics platform and data ecosystem.

Looking ahead, this position offers the opportunity to influence how USAA evolves beyond traditional telematics into a broader connected ecosystem. As connected vehicles, smart devices, sensors, and Internet of Things technologies continue to reshape the industry, USAA is exploring new ways to leverage data to improve member outcomes across both Auto and Property insurance, including Connected Home capabilities designed to proactively help members prevent losses before they occur.

For accomplished technology leaders from leading insurers, telematics providers, connected vehicle platforms, mobility technology companies, or other data-driven organizations, this represents a rare opportunity to move beyond managing an established program and help define the future direction of an increasingly strategic enterprise capability. The successful candidate will influence multi-year business and technology roadmaps, partner directly with senior leaders across technology and the business, and help determine how telematics, artificial intelligence, and emerging data ecosystems shape the future of insurance at USAA.

Few opportunities offer this combination of strategic visibility, technical complexity, business impact, and innovation. The work spans cloud modernization, AI, machine learning, mobile technologies, data engineering, vehicle integrations, digital experiences, pricing, underwriting, claims, and connected-device ecosystems, all within an organization making significant long-term investments in these capabilities.

For executives who are already successful and not actively considering a career move, this opportunity offers something increasingly rare: the chance to build and scale a transformative capability at an organization where telematics is already influencing core business decisions and is expected to play an even larger role in the future. The leader selected for this role will have a unique opportunity to help define how USAA leverages connected data, advanced analytics, and emerging technologies to better serve millions of members and strengthen its competitive position for years to come.

Executive Directors in Application Development plan, coordinate, and supervise all activities related to the design, development, and implementation and maintenance of the organization's applications development and analysis function. These leaders also manage multiple development teams often supporting one or more lines of business or business functional areas. Additionally, these leaders work closely with clients in order to map and support their operational needs. These leaders are also responsible for developing, distributing, supporting, enforcing, and integrating best practices and technology standards across the organization, including ensuring all Information Technology General Controls, processes and procedures are followed as applicable and appropriate.

Location

USAA offers a flexible work environment that requires an individual to be in the office 4 days per week. This position can be based in one of the following locations: Plano, TX (preference) or San Antonio, TX. Relocation assistance is available for this position.

What You'll Do

Perform workload management and prioritization duties in support of operations for the functional area assigned.
Apply subject-matter-expert functional knowledge to lead subordinate workers in producing work deliverables in support of departmental initiatives.
Develop functional policies, procedures and guidelines.
Identify opportunities and facilitates major improvements to processes and systems.
Ensure that the assigned application group develops processes and tools that contribute to the company business objectives.
Ensure that all application processes developed internally or by external service providers are conducted in line with corporate social responsibility, environmental and technical policies and applicable standards and legislation.
Oversee the assessment of the technical and business fitness of the application portfolio and their associated costs and risks In partnership with CTO, Infrastructure and IT Security, and ensure that the organization's applications are effectively secured and that risks are mitigated and comply with legal and corporate privacy and confidentiality rules.
Establish management routines to ensure appropriate oversight of the organization's software development and maintenance activities.
Serve as financial steward for the organization and manage relationships with major vendors and service providers to ensure they cost-effectively meet the needs of the organization.
Evaluate and select third party vendors to provide value added services.
Facilitate the contracting process through the Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) enterprise process.
Responsible for contract company/service performance providing timely feedback to ensure the best value for USAA.
Collaborate with CTO to ensure that solutions are consistent with technology standards.
Work across IT and business partners to reduce technical debt.
Collaborate with other leaders and/or stakeholders and develop an application development strategy that aligns with business strategy, adds value and is within budget constraints.
Responsible for team's adherence to SDLC and applicable controls.
Work to ensure teams have appropriate, development plans consistent with domain of expertise.
Mentor across the technical community.
Provide oversight to the engagement with the business DPO and ensure deliverables adhere to Agile practices / methodologies.
Ensure risks associated with business activities are effectively identified, measured, monitored, and controlled in accordance with risk and compliance policies and procedures.

What You Have

Bachelors degree in Computer Science, I.S., or related field; OR 4 years of relevant education and/or experience.
10 years of experience of general IT management competencies.
4 years of people leadership experience in building, managing and/or developing high-performing teams required.
Strong technical background of web-based application architecture, system and database architecture, security application integration and object-oriented languages in a large enterprise environment.
Experience in all stages of the SDLC: requirements gathering, design, development, testing, and implementation.
Demonstrated ability to communicate technical information to a non-technical audience.
Experience collaborating with resources and stakeholders, influencing decisions and managing work to achieve strategic goals.
Experienced in vendor contract management and management of distributed development teams and resources.
Financial acumen involving budgets, forecasting, and executing on the budgets for applicable technology support function.
Understanding of relevant industry frameworks (e.g., COBIT, ITIL, SAFe, etc.)
Understanding of Legislative and Regulatory Compliance Requirements.
Experience overseeing the technology life cycle from requirements analysis, feasibility estimates, design, code, documentation, testing, implementation, and support.
Technical knowledge and understanding of technical domains that reside within Infrastructure Services, Security, Data or Application Development.
Experience conducting cost benefit analyses and leveraging results to drive technology support solutions.
Demonstrated thought leadership in embedding intuitive story telling of technology support functions including concise presentation of complex technical details.
Experience and ability to drive a culture of quality and personal accountability through technology support teams.

What Sets You Apart

5+ years of experience in behavior and usage-based insurance technology or telematics programs.
3+ years of experience modernizing legacy insurance systems to public cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, GCP, Azure).
Domain experience with usage-based and behavior-based insurance, personal lines insurance, and personal lines claims.
Experience leading the technical strategy and delivery of telematics solutions for P&C, maintaining and building relationships with ecosystem partners, and translating telematic data into higher value using AI.
Experience partnering with business stakeholders in building multi-year roadmaps across P&C functional areas to advance the telematics architecture that supports multi-product capabilities.
Experience scaling data platforms that ingest massive telematics streams (e.g., Mobile app data, IoT device data, OEM vehicle data) and using near real-time data for multiple insurance use cases.
Experience building mobile app experiences tailored to telematic insurance programs.
Experience partnering with key industry telematic suppliers (e.g., CMT, Arity, Okto) or vehicle OEMs.
Experience using machine learning or advanced models to turn telematics data into risk scoring, analytical insights, pricing segmentation, claims detection, or customer engagement tools.
Experience leading the technical strategy to deliver telematic solutions at top insurance carriers.

new_jobs.title: Director of Communications and Marketing
new_jobs.description:
ABOUT THE COMMUNICATIONS AND MARKETING DIRECTOR POSITION

The Communications and Marketing Director for the City of Greensboro is a
dynamic executive leadership role for a strategic communicator who wants to make a meaningful impact on an entire community. This position leads the City’s comprehensive communications and marketing efforts, shaping how residents, businesses, visitors, and stakeholders experience and understand their local government.

Reporting to an Assistant City Manager, the Director will oversee the City’s full spectrum of communications operations — including internal and external communications, marketing, Greensboro Television Network, the contact center, and print shop/mail services. This individual will work directly with elected officials, the City Manager’s Office, and department leaders to develop forward-thinking strategies, address emerging issues, and deliver clear, compelling messages that tell Greensboro’s story with accuracy and transparency.

The Director will elevate and strengthen content creation standards across the organization, setting clear expectations for high-quality, strategic, and consistent communications. This includes overseeing multi-platform writing and digital content production that effectively reaches audiences across websites, email communications, social media channels, video platforms, and emerging digital tools. The Director will ensure messaging is tailored appropriately for each platform while maintaining a cohesive and recognizable City brand voice.

In addition to written communications, the Director will oversee comprehensive digital content production, including multimedia storytelling, visual design standards, video messaging, and web content optimization. The role requires ensuring that content is accessible, engaging, and aligned with best practices in digital communication, including search optimization and usability standards.

A strong candidate will bring a data-driven mindset to the organization. The Communications and Marketing Director will leverage analytical tools and performance metrics to guide strategy, evaluate impact, and inform decision-making. This includes utilizing website and social media analytics, engagement metrics, sentiment analysis, and audience insights to refine messaging and outreach efforts. The Director will oversee proactive social media management strategies, including content planning, scheduling, real-time engagement, performance tracking, and continuous improvement informed by analytics. By grounding communications strategies in data, the Director will ensure resources are allocated effectively and messaging resonates with diverse audiences across the community.

The Director must also demonstrate exceptional skill in translating complex, technical, or policy-driven information into clear, accessible, and audience-centered messaging. Whether communicating budget priorities, infrastructure projects, public safety initiatives, or crisis updates, the Director will ensure that information is presented in ways that are transparent, understandable, and meaningful to residents and stakeholders.

The Communications and Marketing Director will serve as the steward of the City’s brand — ensuring that all messaging strengthens public trust, enhances reputation, and reflects the City’s values and priorities. This includes creating proactive, analytics-informed communications that engage residents, visitors, and business owners, as well as leading communications during high-profile initiatives, major events, and crisis situations with real-time monitoring and strategic responsiveness.

Additionally, the Communications and Marketing Director will provide the vision and strategic leadership to guide the Communications team through change and modernization. The Director will foster a culture of innovation, empowering staff to explore new ideas, communication approaches, and technologies that strengthen the reach and impact of the City’s communications program. Through intentional coaching, mentoring, and professional development, the Director will build staff capabilities and enhance the department’s overall effectiveness.

As a key member of the City Manager’s leadership team, the Director will collaborate across departments and with elected leadership to help shape programs, services, and community initiatives that advance organizational goals and improve quality of life for the people of Greensboro.

This Exempt position offers the opportunity to lead a talented team, influence citywide strategy, and play a central role in building an informed, connected, and engaged community.

ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION

The City of Greensboro is governed under a Council-Manager form of government, with the council serving as the legislative body of City government. City council is composed of a mayor and eight council members who serve four-year terms. The council is responsible for setting and directing policy regarding operations of City government, as well as approving the City’s budget of $909.8M, which supports 3,063 full-time, 59 part-time, and up to 681 temporary and seasonal employees across many departments. The City Manager serves as the chief executive officer of the City and is responsible for the execution of council policy and for the management of day-to-day City government operations.

Learn more about the City of Greensboro by visiting its website.

COMPENSATION INFORMATION

The full salary range for the position is $119,856-$214,479 with eligibility for additional executive compensation of $4,320 annually. As a City employee, the Communications and Marketing Director participates in the North Carolina Local Governmental Employees’ Retirement System (NCLGERS), which includes a 6% pre-tax employee contribution and a City-funded employer contribution, with vesting after five years.

Supplemental retirement savings opportunities include participation in a 401(a) plan with a 3.25% City contribution based on base salary, as well as 457 / Roth 457 and 401(k) / Roth 401(k) plans. For highly experienced executives, the City may recognize prior public sector service through adjusted leave accrual rates and initial leave balances, consistent with established policies. Learn more about the City’s generous benefits package here.

As with all individuals appointed as City Department Directors, the Communications and Marketing Director must live within a 30-mile radius of the Greensboro city limits within 12 months of their appointment.

QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor’s Degree and 7 or more years of experience in communications and marketing, preferably within the non-profit government sector OR Associate’s Degree and 10 or more years of experience in the above mentioned areas
Minimum of 5 years of supervision/management of teams engaged in corporate communications, public relations, video production and/or social media

An Ideal Candidate Would Also Possess (Preferred Qualifications):

Budget management/financial management experience
Municipal government management experience at the senior or executive level
Prior media and publication experience
Expertise in crisis communications
Ability to effectively manage through change, modernization, and departmental transformation

TO APPLY

Please submit your application along with a resume, cover letter, and reference information to the City of Greensboro, NC application located here: Greensboro Communications and Marketing Director Application. The application deadline is October 11th, with final review of applications occurring the week of October 19th.
